key_insight: Quantum simulations designed to compute response functions also prepare many-body states that reveal how information spreads, becomes locally accessible, and supports entanglement.
engineering_relevance: Reusing response-simulation states for quantum-information analysis could broaden the value of existing protocols and guide measurement choices.
method: Study local-pulse Green-function protocols in finite XX and XXX spin chains.
Encode a classical bit with opposite source rotations and track its propagation and local accessibility.
Analyze reduced states for source-angle estimation, Bell-state recovery, communication rates, and entanglement.
evidence_signal: In the studied chains, fermionic covariance data exactly reconstruct the signed XX response, yet simple spin measurements recover a larger fraction of locally available information in XXX; this ordering also holds for local source-angle estimation.
watch_item: The results concern finite spin-chain case studies; scalability and robustness to experimental noise remain unestablished in the abstract.
paper_title: Dynamical quantum simulations as laboratories for quantum information
